title: Fermented Teff Roasted Chicken with Spicy Berbere
summary: This distinctive Ethiopian-inspired entree is built around fermented teff batter, bringing tangy sour notes to roasted poultry. Whole chicken pieces are coated in a fiery paste of berbere spices, grated ginger, minced garlic, and niter kibbeh before roasting on high heat. Underneath the roasting rack, a thin layer of fermented teff batter bakes into a savory sponge-like bread crust that catches every drop of seasoned pan drippings. The natural acidity of fermented teff cuts through the intense heat of dark chili spices and rich poultry fat, creating a complex flavor dynamic. As the chicken roasts to golden perfection with crisp skin, the fermented base underneath turns tender and flavorful. Served alongside tender collard greens sautéed with garlic and onions, this dish offers an authentic taste of East African culinary tradition. It brings together bold aromatic heat, fermented tang, and succulent roasted meat in a single memorable platter perfect for family feasts.

steps.step: Pat chicken parts completely dry with clean kitchen towels to allow spice rub to adhere easily.
Mince red onion, garlic cloves, and fresh ginger root finely on wooden cutting board.
Melt niter kibbeh spiced butter gently in small saucepan over low heat until liquid warm.
Whisk berbere spice blend, ground fenugreek, cardamom, coriander, cloves, and nutmeg together.
Combine melted spiced butter, minced aromatics, spice mixture, salt, and lemon juice into paste.
Rub berbere paste evenly over chicken pieces, pushing marinade under skin for max flavor.
Cover coated chicken in glass bowl and rest at room temperature for thirty minutes to marinate.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit and position oven rack in middle baking slot.
Grease a large metal roasting pan lightly with olive oil to prevent fermented batter sticking.
Pour fermented teff batter evenly into bottom of roasting pan, spreading into thin layer.
Place roasting rack directly over teff batter inside pan to suspend chicken during roasting.
Arrange marinated chicken pieces onto roasting rack skin-side up with space between pieces.
Drizzle remaining berbere paste from bowl over top surface of arranged chicken parts.
Transfer roasting pan carefully into preheated oven, closing door to trap roasting heat.
Roast chicken undisturbed for twenty-five minutes until skin begins to crisp and color.
Prepare collard greens by washing leaves thoroughly and removing thick central woody stems.
Slice collard green leaves into thin ribbons across width using sharp chef knife on board.
Dice jalapeno pepper finely, removing seeds if milder heat level is desired for side dish.
Peel hard boiled eggs and score surface lightly with four shallow vertical knife slashes.
Heat olive oil in wide skillet over medium heat for sautéing collard greens accompaniment.
Add remaining minced onion and garlic to hot oil, cooking until soft and lightly golden brown.
Add collard greens and chicken broth to skillet, simmering covered for fifteen minutes until soft.
Baste chicken pieces with juices dripped onto teff layer using kitchen spoon halfway through cook.
Continue roasting chicken for twenty-five additional minutes until internal temp reaches 165 degrees.
Verify teff batter underneath has baked into porous fermented bread crust absorbing chicken juices.
Remove roasting pan from oven carefully using heavy oven mitts and place on heatproof surface.
Transfer roasted chicken pieces to warm resting platter and tent loosely with aluminum foil.
Let chicken rest ten minutes to allow savory juices to redistribute throughout meat fibers.
Stir cider vinegar, black cumin seeds, and jalapeno into cooked collard greens in skillet.
Add scored hard boiled eggs into collard greens, rolling them gently in pan juices to warm.
Season greens with salt and paprika, stirring well over low heat for two final minutes.
Cut baked fermented teff bread crust from pan floor into broad square serving pieces.
Lay warm fermented teff bread pieces flat across bottom of large traditional serving platter.
Arrange roasted berbere chicken pieces neatly over center of fermented teff bread base.
Spoon cooked collard greens around chicken, placing warm hard boiled eggs at platter corners.
Drizzle any remaining seasoned roasting juices from pan over chicken and teff bread layer.
Garnish platter with fresh chopped cilantro leaves and extra sprinkle of berbere spice powder.
Serve immediately while roasted chicken remains piping hot and teff base is tender and warm.
Provide extra warm teff flatbreads on side plate for tearing and scooping meat and greens.
Carve chicken pieces at table if needed to make serving easier for dining guests.
Offer fresh lemon wedges alongside platter for diners who want extra bright tartness.
Store leftover chicken and teff bread separately in chilled containers for up to two days.
Reheat leftover chicken in hot oven to crisp skin while warming teff bread in covered pan.
